summary.oneLiner: Datamatics delivered strong Q2FY26 growth with 20.5% YoY revenue and 82.2% EBITDA growth, driven by operational efficiencies and AI investments, despite Digital Experiences softness from one client transition; the sustained margin expansion and healthy cash position signal structural improvement and readiness for accelerated growth.

one-line thesis: Datamatics delivered strong Q2FY26 growth with 20.5% YoY revenue and 82.2% EBITDA growth, driven by operational efficiencies and AI investments, despite Digital Experiences softness from one client transition; the sustained margin expansion and healthy cash position signal structural improvement and readiness for accelerated growth.
financial scorecard: Revenue: +20.5% YoY (Rs. 490.2cr); EBITDA: +82.2% YoY (Rs. 88.8cr), margin 18.1% (+613 bps YoY); PAT (reported): +49.3% YoY (Rs. 63.2cr); PAT (normalized): same (no one-offs); order book: not disclosed; net debt: net cash of Rs. 509.4cr (cash-rich)
guidance: Revenue growth: mid-teens FY26 (incl. acquisitions); EBITDA margin: sustainable at current levels; order inflow: expected recovery in Digital Experiences; capex/commissioning: no capex disclosed, R&D spend Rs. 40-50cr annually expensed
segment / subsidiary detail: Digital Technologies: Rs. 153.1cr (+6.1% QoQ), EBIT margin 10.8%; Digital Operations: Rs. 272.5cr (+6.6% QoQ), EBIT margin 16.7%; Digital Experiences: Rs. 64.6cr (-4.4% QoQ), EBIT margin 10.8% (improved but facing one client transition by Dec 2025)
growth verticals / optionality: Expansion in U.S./Europe via strengthened sales teams; cross-selling AI products (TruBot, TruCap+, FINATO) to existing clients; hyperscaler partnerships (Microsoft, Google, Salesforce); potential acquisition upside if targets materialize
margins & cost dynamics: Margin expansion driven by operational efficiencies, lean cost structure, pricing discipline, and AI-driven productivity gains; cost optimization ongoing across all segments; Digital Experiences margin improvement offset by client transition risk
capex / expansion: No capex disclosed; Rs. 40-50cr annually invested in AI/R&D, fully expensed (not capitalized), primarily in Digital Technologies
capital allocation: Net cash of Rs. 509.4cr; no active acquisitions in pipeline; focus on organic growth and R&D; potential for future M&A if strategic targets emerge
risks & watch-items: One key client transition in Digital Experiences (Q3FY26); reliance on Western markets (77% revenue); AI investment not capitalized, impacting reported margins; potential delay in Agentic workflow adoption due to compliance constraints
management quality / tone: Confident and disciplined; focused on sustainability, operational excellence, and AI leadership; transparent about challenges (client transition) and optimistic on recovery; no overpromising on growth targets
non-obvious takeaways: Rs. 40-50cr annual R&D spend is fully expensed — if capitalized, EBITDA margin would be ~22-23%; AI products are embedded in solutions, not separately tracked, masking true product revenue contribution; client concentration is healthy (top 20 = 52%) despite market softness
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Client transition in Digital Experiences | Datamatics Global Services Limited | loser | High | Q3FY26 revenue and margin may dip temporarily; recovery depends on new logo wins and backlog fill |

themes.title: AI-led IT services & ER&D transformation
themes.need: Q1FY27 split the bucket three ways: a soft large-cap core, a re-accelerating mid-cap tier, and an outright business-model change. TCS grew constant currency only +0.4% QoQ / +3.2% YoY despite $9.5bn of TCV (including an ~$800mn net-new SKF mega-deal), and its AI-services book annualising $2.6bn (+13.6% QoQ) saw incremental adds DECELERATE from +$125mn to +$75mn - AI is still project revenue, not annuity. WIPRO is the laggard (+0.9% YoY cc, margin -120bps to 16.0%, Q2 guided -1.5% to +0.5%). Mid-caps are outgrowing: TECHM grew +6.6% YoY cc with every vertical up and an 11th consecutive quarter of margin expansion (14.4%, +330bps); MPHASIS's pipeline is at an all-time high, 2.8x its size at the Mphasis.ai launch and +28% YoY, with AI-led deals now 70% of it (from 12%) and BFS pipeline +100% YoY, and its new Tria platform closed multiple opportunities within seven weeks of launch; FRACTAL lifted net income +92% YoY on INR 912.5cr revenue at NRR 117% with zero churn (though only +9% cc, dragged by TMT -22%); KPITTECH won $349M of new deals with 21% of pipeline now productized AI/SDV solutions. Structurally, HCLTECH is entering the AI-datacenter business with an initial investment of up to INR 3,500cr and a 50MW long-term ambition, and PERSISTENT is buying Nagarro at EUR 1.27bn EV to build a $2.9bn / 46,000-person group - European scale is now bought, not built. The new cost line is visas: TATAELXSI crossed INR 1,000cr of quarterly revenue for the first time (INR 1,021.1cr) yet EBIT fell 330bps QoQ, with 220-230bps of it onsite/subcontractor investment the CFO said cannot be passed to customers.
themes.driver: MPHASIS's guide that 'Q2 is positioned to deliver the best sequential constant currency growth we have delivered in three years' is the most falsifiable claim in the sector; then HCLTECH's AI-datacenter build, the PERSISTENT-Nagarro close, and whether TCS's AI incremental adds re-accelerate off +$75mn.
